course_description:
Independent research thesis on a selected topic within the area of discipline interest. Research is supervised by one or two academic staff members. Students commencing in Semester 1 enrol in RBUS6996 in both semesters. Students commencing in Semester 2 enrol in RBUS6997 in both semesters.

The aim of the research thesis is to provide the opportunity to learn how to conduct high-quality rigorous research. Students undertake an independent research thesis, enabling them to explore a specific area of interest. In completing the research thesis, students are exposed to the entire research process, from selecting a topic and formulating research questions to conducting a literature review, developing hypotheses (if applicable), designing a methodology, analysing data, and interpreting results. Students work closely with an academic advisor to refine their research proposals, receive feedback, and ensure academic rigour.

timetable:
Additional timetable information
This thesis is an Independent Research Activity (Independent Study), and will not have any regular classes.
We encourage you to contact your Academic Supervisor as soon as possible to discuss your research timeline, setup milestones (or goals) to meet throughout the semester and ensure regular meetings have been scheduled to review your progress. Your supervisor will be your first point of contact.
course_aims: The aim of the research thesis is to provide the opportunity to learn how to conduct high quality rigorous research under academic supervision.

learning_outcomes.description: Explain advanced knowledge of the field of study, informed by current research, theory, and scholarly debate.
Propose justified research problems within the field and rigorous research questions and/or hypotheses.
Conduct a substantial research project by applying appropriate methodologies in a systematic, critical, and evidence-based manner.
Evaluate appropriate analysis techniques and software to analyse research data, synthesising findings to draw coherent and well-justified conclusions.
Communicate research rationale, methods, and outcomes at an advanced scholarly level using discipline-appropriate conventions and technologies.
Address social and ethical considerations throughout the research process by applying relevant ethical standards.

assessment_details.title: Honours Thesis
assessment_details.task_description: The empirical honours thesis follows the same basic format as an empirical masters thesis or PhD thesis. To that end, unless otherwise instructed by the supervisor, the empirical honours thesis will have a minimum chapter content likely to include: Introduction Literature review Model and hypotheses Methodology of data collection Analysis, results and discussion Conclusion The above structure is an example for an empirical thesis. In cases where a theoretical thesis is undertaken, a different structure would be required. Students are advised to seek direction of their supervisor on the appropriate structure in such cases. Additional information related to the format, word count, ethics requirements and submission details can be found on the course Blackboard site. Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.due_date: 24/05/2027 1:00 pm Five check-ins must be completed and submitted via Blackboard by Monday of Week 26, before 1:00 pm. You are responsible for working with your supervisor to schedule these check-ins across the two semesters.
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment is a series of structured sessions designed to help you steadily advance your research. These check-ins let you regularly reflect on your progress, clarify your ideas, and receive formative feedback. Through these check-ins, you should demonstrate active engagement with your research. This may include refining your research questions, developing your literature review, planning or conducting data work, and reflecting on challenges as well as next steps. Ideally, the five check-ins should be spaced evenly across two semesters. For example, two of the five check-ins should be completed in your enrolling semester. Before each meeting, complete the research progress check-in template (available on Blackboard), which will help you reflect on your progress, identify challenges, and structure a focused and productive discussion with your supervisor.
Note: The template is intended as a guide only. You may go beyond the template where relevant and raise any additional questions, ideas, or concerns you would like to discuss.
Once all five check-ins are completed, please upload these five check-in documents as a single PDF document to Blackboard by Week 26 Monday before 1pm.
